# Analysis of Flood Impact on Population and Development Indicators

## Loading packages

```{r}
# Set up renv for package management
if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("renv")
} else {
    message("renv is already installed.")
}

# Load the renv package
library(renv)

# Check if renv is already active, activate if not
if (!renv::status()$synchronized) {
    renv::activate()
}

# To restore the environment (for a collaborator)
renv::restore()

# Load packages
library(terra)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)
library(rasterVis)
library(tidyterra)
library(patchwork)
library(here)

library(factoextra)

```

## Data Loading and Handling

```{r}
# Define folder path and load raster files
folder_path_dev <- here("Data", "processed", "Worldpop_dev_indicators")
tif_files_dev <- list.files(folder_path_dev, pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)

# Load the mean raster files
raster_data_mean <- c(
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("ANC_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("INSURANCE_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("MALNUTRITION_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("PNC_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("SBA_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("TT_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("DECISION_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("HWEALTH_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("MEDUCATION_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("UGA_HSIZE_MEAN", tif_files_dev)])
)

# Load all raster layers  using the rast function
raster_data_dev <- lapply(tif_files_dev, rast)

# Load population raster file
KAMP_POPULATION_10m <- rast(here("Data", "processed", "Worldpop_density", "pop_total_10m.tif"))
```

## Aligning Rasters to Population Data and Naming
```{r}
# Align the rasters to the population raster
aligned_rasters <- lapply(raster_data_dev, function(r) {
  Spatial.align::align(r, KAMP_POPULATION_10m, resample_method = "near")
})

# Extract names of each SpatRaster and assign them to the list
raster_names <- sapply(aligned_rasters, names)

# Assign these names to the list
names(aligned_rasters) <- raster_names

# Removed HSIZE as a PCA without it was more interpretable
aligned_rasters <- aligned_rasters[-grep("UGA_HSIZE_MEAN", raster_names)]

# Remove redundant objects
# rm(raster_data_dev, tif_files_dev, KAMP_POPULATION_10m, folder_path_dev, raster_names)
```

## Plotting Histograms and Rasters of Development Indicators
```{r}
# Set up a plotting layout (adjust nrows and ncols as needed)
par(mfrow = c(3, 3))  # Example: 3x3 grid for 9 histograms

# Loop through the list and plot histograms with all raster values and names
for (i in seq_along(aligned_rasters)) {
  hist(aligned_rasters[[i]], 
       main = paste("Histogram of", raster_names[i]), 
       col = "skyblue", border = "black", maxcell = Inf)
}

# Loop through the rasters and plot each one
for (i in seq_along(aligned_rasters)) {
  plot(aligned_rasters[[i]], 
       main = paste("Raster", raster_names[i]), 
       col = terrain.colors(100))
}

# Reset plotting layout to default
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# PCA Analysis
```{r}
# #################### Step 1: Convert Rasters to Dataframe ####################
# Convert aligned SpatRaster objects into a single raster stack
vulnerability_stack <- rast(aligned_rasters)

df <- as.data.frame(vulnerability_stack, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

# Store XY coordinates separately
xy_coords <- df[, c("x", "y")]

# Remove XY coordinates from the dataframe before analysis
df <- df[, !(colnames(df) %in% c("x", "y"))]

# #################### Step 2: Visualize Outliers Using Boxplots ####################
# boxplot(df, main = "Boxplots of Variables")  

# #################### Step 3: Perform KMO Test and Remove Low-MSA Variables ####################
perform_kmo <- function(df, max_iterations = 10) {
  iteration <- 0
  thresholds <- seq(0.1, 0.5, by = 0.1)  # Gradually increase the threshold

  for (threshold in thresholds) {
    repeat {
      kmo_results <- KMO(df)
      print(kmo_results)

      message("Iteration: ", iteration, " | Threshold: ", threshold)
      print(kmo_results$MSAi)

      if (all(kmo_results$MSAi >= threshold)) break

      vars_to_remove <- names(kmo_results$MSAi)[kmo_results$MSAi < threshold]
      df <- df[, !(colnames(df) %in% vars_to_remove)]

      message("Removing variables with MSAi < ", threshold, ": ", paste(vars_to_remove, collapse = ", "))

      iteration <- iteration + 1
      if (iteration >= max_iterations) break
    }
  }
  return(df)
}

# Apply KMO filtering
df <- perform_kmo(df)

# #################### Step 4: Compute Correlation Matrix ####################
cor_matrix <- cor(df, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
print(cor_matrix)

# Conduct Bartlett's test for sphericity (ensures PCA is valid)
bartlett_test <- cortest.bartlett(cor_matrix, n = nrow(df))
print(bartlett_test)

# #################### Step 5: Check Multicollinearity ####################
# Check determinant of correlation matrix (should not be close to 0)
det_value <- det(cor_matrix)
print(det_value)  

# Compute Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) to detect multicollinearity
df <- as.data.frame(df)  # Convert to data frame

vif_values <- apply(df, 2, function(x) {
  lm_model <- lm(x ~ ., data = df)
  return(vif(lm_model))
})
print(vif_values)

# #################### Step 6: Conduct PCA with Oblimin Rotation and Kaiser Normalization ####################
# Run PCA with oblimin rotation and Kaiser normalization
pca_result_1 <- principal(df, 
              nfactors = 1,    # Choose based on eigenvalues >1 or scree plot
              rotate = "oblimin", 
              scores = TRUE, 
              normalize = TRUE) # Applies Kaiser normalization

# Print PCA results
print(pca_result_1)

pca_result_2 <- principal(df, 
              nfactors = 2, 
              rotate = "oblimin", 
              scores = TRUE, 
              normalize = TRUE)

print(pca_result_2)

pca_result_3 <- principal(df, 
              nfactors = 3, 
              rotate = "oblimin", 
              scores = TRUE, 
              normalize = TRUE)

print(pca_result_3)

# Merge XY coordinates back to the PCA scores
pca_scores_with_xy <- cbind(xy_coords, as.data.frame(pca_result_3$scores))

# Convert PCA scores back into a raster stack
pca_raster <- rast(pca_scores_with_xy)

autoplot(pca_raster, main = "PCA Scores (3 Components)")

# #################### Interpretation ####################

# Variable Selection Based on KMO and Variance:
# - The Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) test was performed iteratively to ensure factorability.
# - Variables with MSA (Measure of Sampling Adequacy) < 0.5 were removed.
# - The final retained variables for PCA analysis are:
#   - UGA_INSURANCE_MEAN (KMO = 0.58)
#   - UGA_MALNUTRITION_MEAN (KMO = 0.89)
#   - UGA_MEDUCATION_MEAN (KMO = 0.87)
#   - UGA_SBA_MEAN (KMO = 0.58)

# Multicollinearity Check:
# - The determinant of the correlation matrix is 0.235, indicating an acceptable level of collinearity.
# - Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) values:
#   - UGA_INSURANCE_MEAN: 3.44
#   - UGA_MALNUTRITION_MEAN: 1.22
#   - UGA_MEDUCATION_MEAN: 1.07
#   - UGA_SBA_MEAN: 3.29
# - Since all VIF values are below 5, no severe multicollinearity is detected.

# PCA Results:
# - **1-Component Model:**
#   - Explains 55% of the variance.
#   - High loadings on UGA_INSURANCE_MEAN (0.92) and UGA_SBA_MEAN (0.90).
#   - RMSR = 0.14, suggesting a moderate fit.

# - **2-Component Model:**
#   - Explains 78% of the variance cumulatively.
#   - Component 1 (TC1) is linked to **financial and maternal health services**.
#   - Component 2 (TC2) is associated with **education and decision-making**.
#   - The component correlation (0.16) indicates mild interdependence.

# - **3-Component Model:**
#   - Explains 96% of the variance cumulatively.
#   - The components align clearly:
#     - **TC1:** Healthcare access (UGA_INSURANCE_MEAN, UGA_SBA_MEAN).
#     - **TC2:** Educational status (UGA_MEDUCATION_MEAN).
#     - **TC3:** Nutritional vulnerability (UGA_MALNUTRITION_MEAN).
#   - RMSR = 0.03, suggesting a very good model fit.

# Interpretation of Rotated Components (Oblimin Rotation):
# - **Component 1 (Healthcare & Financial Accessibility):**
#   - Strongly associated with **UGA_INSURANCE_MEAN (0.94)** and **UGA_SBA_MEAN (0.97)**.
#   - Represents **access to health insurance and skilled birth attendance**.
# 
# - **Component 2 (Education & Decision-Making):**
#   - Driven by **UGA_MEDUCATION_MEAN (1.00)**.
#   - Reflects **higher maternal education and its influence on decision-making**.
#
# - **Component 3 (Nutritional Status & Vulnerability):**
#   - Captured solely by **UGA_MALNUTRITION_MEAN (1.00)**.
#   - Highlights **malnutrition as a distinct factor in vulnerability**.
# ########################################################
```

## Computing the PCA-based index
```{r}
# Define updated weights based on variance explained
weights <- c(0.48, 0.26, 0.26)  # Weights for PC1, PC2, PC3

# Compute weighted index as a linear combination of PCA scores
pca_index <- (weights[1] * pca_result_3$scores[, 1]) +
             (weights[2] * pca_result_3$scores[, 2]) +
             (weights[3] * pca_result_3$scores[, 3])

# Convert PCA index to a data frame
pca_index_df <- data.frame(xy_coords, pca_index)

# Convert PCA index back to a raster
pca_index <- rast(pca_index_df)

# Plot the PCA-Based Vulnerability Index with turbo color scheme
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = pca_index, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo", name = "PCA Index", na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(title = "PCA-Based Vulnerability Index",
       subtitle = "Computed from Principal Component Analysis",
       caption = "Data Source: Worldpop Development Indicators") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 8),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90")) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 1, barheight = 20))

# Define quantile breaks (5 equal groups)
quantile_breaks <- quantile(pca_index_df$pca_index, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 6), na.rm = TRUE)

# Assign each raster cell to a quantile category
pca_index_df$quantile <- cut(pca_index_df$pca_index, breaks = quantile_breaks, labels = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)

# Convert quantile column back to raster
pca_quantile_raster <- rast(pca_index_df[, c("x", "y", "quantile")])

# factorize
pca_quantile_raster <- as.factor(pca_quantile_raster)

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = pca_quantile_raster, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "1" = "#1a9850",  # Very Low Vulnerability (Green)
    "2" = "#66bd63",  # Low Vulnerability (Light Green)
    "3" = "#ffffbf",  # Vulnerable (Yellow)
    "4" = "#fdae61",  # Moderately Vulnerable (Orange)
    "5" = "#d7191c"   # Highly Vulnerable (Red)
  ), 
  labels = c(
    "1" = "Very Low Vulnerability", 
    "2" = "Low Vulnerability", 
    "3" = "Vulnerable", 
    "4" = "Moderately Vulnerable", 
    "5" = "Highly Vulnerable"
  ), 
  name = "Vulnerability Scale", na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(title = "PCA-Based Vulnerability Index (Likert Scale)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", 
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        axis.title.y = element_blank()) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(na.translate = FALSE)))

# load the administrative boundaries by running 01.1_loading_processed_data.qmd
# Plot the PCA-based vulnerability index with administrative boundaries
plot_quantile_parishes_index = ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = pca_quantile_raster, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_spatvector(data = Adm_boundaries, color = "black", fill = NA) +
  geom_spatvector_text(data = Adm_boundaries, aes(label = PName2016), 
                       size = 3, color = "black", check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "1" = "#1a9850",  # Very Low Vulnerability (Green)
    "2" = "#66bd63",  # Low Vulnerability (Light Green)
    "3" = "#ffffbf",  # Vulnerable (Yellow)
    "4" = "#fdae61",  # Moderately Vulnerable (Orange)
    "5" = "#d7191c"   # Highly Vulnerable (Red)
  ), 
  labels = c(
    "1" = "Very Low Vulnerability", 
    "2" = "Low Vulnerability", 
    "3" = "Vulnerable", 
    "4" = "Moderately Vulnerable", 
    "5" = "Highly Vulnerable"
  ), 
  name = "Vulnerability Scale", na.value = "transparent") +
  labs(title = "PCA-Based Vulnerability Index (Likert Scale)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", 
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)) + # Ensure full white background
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80"), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "grey90")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(na.translate = FALSE)))
```
